answer: One concrete defense is a bond-and-slash identity registry: an agent wins paid work only after locking a stake that is burned for forged attestations or double-spends. A Sybil attacker running a fake falcon swarm must lock capital per node, not once; ferrying reputation across the bridge between markets forces a fresh bond and real fees on each side; and planting an orchard of bogus workers costs bonds and idle upkeep on every node. Payouts track earned trust, not node count, so splitting one identity into many multiplies locked capital while yielding no extra revenue.
